 Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

attendance by City Council Members is $650 monthly regardless of the amount of meetings.

Public Hearings

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including

  3
 Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will

  7
 call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT  N0.  2 TO  CONTRACT  N0.  3542  WITH  NATIONWIDE
  ENVIRONMENT  AL  SERVICES  TO  INCLUDE  ADDITIONAL  STREETS  TO  STREET
  SWEEPING  SERVICES

  PURPOSE:  Nationwide  Environmental  provides  street sweeping  services  citywide.
  Amendment  No. 2 is necessary  to incorporate  Park Place and Park Avenue  to the contract,  at no
  additional  cost to the City.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No.  2 to Contract  No. 3542 ("Agreement")  with Nationwide
  Environmental  Services  to amend  the list of streets where street sweeping services will be
  provided  to include  Park Place and Park Avenue;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  Amendment  No.  2 in a form  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General  Fund.  Amendment  No.  2 incorporates
  the Park Place and Park Avenue streets into the Agreement  at no additional  cost to the City.

  ANALYSIS:  Under  the Agreement,  Nationwide  Environmental  Services  is required  to provide
  street sweeping  services  for the City's  entire  roadway  network.
  The roadway network  identified
  in the contract,  inadvertently  excluded  Park Place and Park Avenue. Amendment  No. 2 will add
  the two  streets to the contract  at no additional cost to the City by expanding Exhibit  B to include
  Park  Place  and Park  Avenue  for  street  sweeping  on the Monday  schedrile  between  12:00  p.m.
  and 4:00 p.m.

  BACKGROUND:  The  Public  Works  Department  provides  street  sweeping  through
  Nationwide  Environmental  Services.  Street  sweeping  services  include  sweeping  of  streets,
  alleyways,  parking  lots, for special  events  and emergency  services.

  The City  Council  approved  the Agreement  with  Nationwide  Environmental  Services  on July  9,
  2019,  for  an amount  not-to-exceed  $3,435,809. Although  the contract  was awarded  on July  9,
  2019,  Contract  No.  3542  was fully  executed  on October  17, 2019,  and services  commenced  on
  October  23, 2019.

  3.  Debris - All litter, rubbish, organic debris including leaves and grass clippings, sand,
  dirt, garbage and other foreign  material  removable  from a paved street with a
  mechanical street sweeper.
  4.  Emergency  (As-needed) Services - Sweeping required by City excluding  regularly
  scheduled street sweeping that requires additional dedicated labor, equipment and work
  hours. Billing for emergency sweeps will be based on an hourly rate with travel time
  excluded.
  5.  Fully  Operational - In a  condition  to  undertake  the  function  to  adequately
  complete sweeping schedules.
  6.  Inclement  Weather  - Weather conditions  that  prohibit  the effective  operation  of
  sweeping  operations,  such as heavy rain or winds.

  excluded.
  8.  Parking  Lots - Asphalt,  concrete or other hard surfaced  areas primarily  for the parking
  of automobiles.

  conducted by City.
  10 , Quality of Sweeping - The street sweeper shall leave designated  areas of sweeping  free
  of all dirt, litter, debris, and visual dust.
  11 , Re-Sweeps - Sweeping required  of Contractor  when previous  sweeps have been
  deemed by City to be of poor quality, or when  a street or sections of a street have
  been missed by Contractor  during  regularly  scheduled street sweeping.  Re-sweeps
  are completed  at the expense of  Contractor  and shall be completed  within 24-
  hours of notice, weather permitting.

  13 . Special Event  Sweeps - Sweeping before  and after special city events. These sweeps
  are included in the contracted service level.

  limits of the City that are paved, whether curbed with or without gutters or uncurbed.

EXISTING  OPERATION

The City is located in the Gateway Cities region of southeastern Los Angeles County with an
estimated current population of 98,633. It is the 17" largest city in the County, located 7 miles
firom Downtown Los Angcles. The City covers an area of approximately 7.5 square miles.

The City's street sweeping operation is managed by the Street and Sewer Division of the Public
Works Department. Sweeping services are currently provided by City employees and utilizing its
own equipment. The City is seeking to provide these services tmough a contract with a sweeping
contractor.

The City has approximately 125 miles of streets, 12 miles of alleys, or an equivalent of 17,976
lane miles per year. In addition, there are approximately 1,500 lane miles per year of street
medians. Residential streets are swept during daytime hours once per week, Commercial,
industrial streets, school areas, and alleys are swept at night once per week. Street medians are
swept two times a week at night. Sweeping services are performed on all holidays. Exhibit A -
Part 2, Table I shows the approximate route miles for the City's street sweeping program.

Sweeping is coordinated with refuse collection, which is provided pursuant to an agreement with
Waste Management Inc., the City's waste hauler. Waste Management Inc., collecti the sweeping
debris deposited at the transfer station located at 9599 Salt Lake Avenue, South Gate 90280 at no
charge. This arrangement is expected to continue. The street sweeper, to the extent possible,
follows the refuse collection vehicle. Each year, the City provides sweeping support to three
special events, All events require a pre-event sweep and post-event sweep to remove debris, For
costing purpose, City has included a three additional events to the list, which is to be detemnined
in the future.

Residential strcets have posted parking restrictions of four (4) hours, between 7:30 am and 4:30
pm. Cars are required to be removed from streets during those time periods posted for street
sweeping. Parking enforcement personnel follow the sweepers and cite vehicles that obstnuct
street sweeping efforts. The successful contractor will coordinate with the Police Department on
routing and service delivery to ensure effective enforcement.

The City is interested in making improvements to its existing program by reducing parking
restrictions in residential neighborhoods from four hours to two hours. The City expects the
successful Contractor to formulate and implement the changes, Revised parking restrictions will
require the selectcd Contractor to purchase and install new signage in the residential
neighborhoods. As described in Exhibit A, some of the signage materials currently in possession

  SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  TIJNITED  PACIFIC  SERVICES,  INC.,  FOR
  CITYWIDE  TREE  MAINTENANCE  SERVICES

  PURPOSE:  The  City  manages  a tree inventory  of over  17,500  trees with  the services  of a
  specialty  tree maintenance  contractor.  Staff  is recommending  awarding  a four-year  agreement  to
  United  Pacific  Services,  Inc. (UPS),  to complete  Year  3 and Year  4 of the ongoing  4-Year  grid
  trim  cycle  and to begin  Year 1 and Year 2 of the next grid trim  cycle.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an agreement with United Pacific Services, Inc. for annual tree maintenance
  services  for a four-year  term in an amount not-to-exceed of $3,789,545;
  b.  Appropriating  an additional  $37,500 in General Funds for Park Tree Maintenance  into
  AccountNo.  100-460-61-6101;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to  the  City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  Proposed  Agreement  is in the  amount  of $3,789,545  and will  be
  funded  with  General  Funds  and Street  Lighting  and Landscape  Funds  budgeted  annually,  as
  summarized  below.  The appropriation  proposed  is $37,500  from  the General  Funds  to fully  fund
  services  for the Parks  and Recreation  Division,  which  are currently  budgeted  in the amount  of
  $90,000  from  General  Funds.

  ANALYSIS:  The  City  owns  a tree inventory  of over  17,500  trees located  on public  streets,
  municipal  facilities,  and municipal  parks.  A Request  for Proposal  (RFP)  was issued  to procure  a
  contractor  for  tree maintenance  services.  Six proposals  were  received,  of which  five  qualified

 contractors  were  invited  to interviews.  Of the five  contractors  scheduled  to interview,  only  four
participated.  The  interview  panel  consisted  of  the  Field  Operations  Manager,  Park
Superintendent,  and  the  Streets  and  Sewer  Superintendent.  The  contractor  selection  criteria
weighed  factors  such  as experience,  costs,  safety  records,  references,  familiarity  with  City
maintenance  standards,  etc. United  Pacific  Services  (UPS)  received  the highest  ranking  from  the

their best and lowest  offer  by August  11, 2022.  After  the deadline,  the City  received  two revised
bids  from  United  Pacific  Services,  Inc.  and Mariposa  Landscape,  Inc.  United  Pacific  Services

by UPS  for a new Revised Proposal Amount  of $3,789,545,  which included  an increase of 100
trees for Bid Item No. 5. Even with the updated quantities,  United Pacific Services is the lowest,
highest ranked bidder for tree maintenance services.

BACKGROUND:  The Public  Works  Department  is responsible  for maintenance  of the City's
urban  forest  consisting  of  approximately  17,500  trees  located  along  roadways,  municipal
facilities,  and parks.  The  City's  tree  maintenance  contract  with  WCA  (Contract  No.  3243)
expired  on July 31, 2021.

Under  Contract  No.  3243,  the City  maintained  its urban  forest  on a 3-year  grid  trim  cycle.
Accordingly,  WCA  provided  services  to complete  a 3-year  grid  trim  cycle.  WCA  was awarded
Amendment  No. 1 to complete  Year 1 of the next 3-year  grid trim  cycle.  Two  years remained  to
complete  the 3-year  grid  trim  cycle;  however,  the City  was impacted  financially  as a result  of
COVID-19.  As a cost-savings  measure,  staff proposed  that the remaining  two years of the 3-year
cycle  be completed  in three  years,  thereby  converting  the 3-year  to a 4-year  grid  trim  cycle,
which  was to reduce  costs by approximately  $157,597  in Fiscal  Year 2021/22  and reduce  aru'iual

  cycle.

  It is important  to note that work  on the 4-year  cycle  has not been completed.  WCA  performed
  Year  1 and Year  2 services;  however,  Year  3 and Year  4 services  have not been completed.  As
  such,  the proposed  UPS  Agreement  provides  services  to complete  Year  3 and Year  4 of the
  ongoing  4-year  tree trimming  cycle,  and to begin  Year  1 and Year  2 services  of the next  tree
  trimming  cycle.  Below  is a summary  of the status of the transition  from  the 3-Year  to the 4-Year

 SUBJECT:  FUNDING  APPROPRIATION  AND  AGREEMENT  WITH  NR
 DEVELOPMENT,  INC.  FOR THE CONSTRUCTION  OF HOLLYDALE  COMMUNITY
 PARK, CITY PROJECT  NO. 607-Pa

 PURPOSE:  The Hollydale  Community  Park Project  is a part of the Capital  Improvement
 Program.  Design  is complete  and construction  bids have been opened.  It is recommended  to
 award  an agreement to NR Development,  Inc. for construction  of the project,  as well  as  to
 program  additional funds for the construction  phase.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
 a.  Approving  Agreement  with NR Development,  Inc.  ("Agreement"),  for the construction
  of Hollydale  Cornrnunity  Park, City Project No. 607-PRK  ("Project"),  in an amount  not-
  to-exceed  $4,899,816;
 b.  Transfering  $1,600,000  in  State  grant  funding  from  Account  No.  311-790-61-9217
  (Circle  Park  Rehabilitation)  to Account  No.  311-790-61-9220  (Hollydale  Community
  Park) to fund the construction  of the Hollydale  Community  Park Project  and authorizing
  the Director of Administrative  Services to make the appropriate  budget adjustments  to the
  revenue  and expenditure accounts;
 C.  Appropriating  $285,000 from the Proposition A Fund to Account  No. 311-790-61-9220
  to fund the construction of the Hollydale Community Park Project;  and
 d.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund. The proposed  Agreement  is in the
 amount  of $4,899,816,  which  is proposed  to be funded  with  $4,153,606  in Proposition  68 Grant
 Funds  and  $746,210  in  State  Grant  Funds.  The  proposed  construction  phase  budget  is
 $6,043,942,  to  be funded  with  $4,158,942  in  Proposition  68  Grant  Funds,  $285,000  in
 Proposition  A Funds, and $1,600,000  in State Grant Funds earmarked  by the Office  of California
 Assembly  Speaker Anthony  Rendon.  The proposed  appropriation  is in the amount  of $285,000
 in Proposition  A Funds to Account No. 311-790-61-9220.  The proposed transfer is $1,600,000
 in State Grant Funds from Account No. 311-790-61-9217  to Account No. 311-790-61-9220.

 ANALYSIS:  The proposed  contract  was procured  through  a competitive  process.  Construction
 was advertised  for bids  and NR  Development,  Inc.,  submitted  the lowest  bid of $4,899,816.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is in the FY 2022/23  CIP.  The Project  is being  implemented  to
renovate  the park.  The  proposed  improvements  include  a 1,700  square-foot  building,  storm
water  chambers,  a playground,  synthetic  turf,  a sand and water  play  area, basketball  court  shade
structures,  a new  irrigation  system,  decomposed  granite,  a park  bench  and  picnic  tables,
permeable  pavers,  concrete  flat work,  and other  miscellaneous  park  amenities.  The design  phase
is complete.  The engineer's  estimate  was $3,338,750.

On June 30, 2022,  staff advertised  the Notice  Inviting  Bids  for construction  in the Daily  Journal.
The Project  was also advertised  on the City's  website  and Ebidboard.  On July 26, 2022,  the City
held a bid opening  at the City  Clerk's  Office.  Five (5) bids were received,  as summarized  below.

  No.  Contactor  Base Bid  Amount

  NR Development,  Inc.  $4,899,816
  MCEC  Inc.  $5,441,330
  Newman  Midland  Corp.  $6,635,218
  Los Angeles  Engineering  Inc.  $7,968,800
  Nationwide  Contracting  Services  $8,145,193

NR Development,  Inc.'s  bid was $4,900,500;  however,  their  bid had an irregularity  which  was a
mathematical  error.  The actual  bid was $4,899,816.  The bid irregularity  was waived  and did not
change the status of NR Development  as the low bidder.

NR Development,  Inc.,  is based in the City  of Downey.  The company  has been in business  for
over seven years.  NR  Development,  Inc.,  has experience  in the City  as they  are the contractor
for the Urban  Orchard  Project,  which  is currently  under  construction.

Pursuant  to the guidelines  of the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  this Project  is
categorically  exempt  under  Title  14 of the California  Code of Regulations,  Section  15302,  Class
2 (Replacement  or Reconstruction)  provides  for an exemption  for minor  alteration  to land, which
was filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Clerk/Registrar-Recorder  on July 19, 2019.

  2

  223
 Construction  is scheduled  to begin  in October  2022 and is scheduled  to be completed  in August
2023.

THIS  ADDENDUM  N0.  1 ("Addendum")  is hereby  made  a part  of  the  above-referenced
agreement  ("Contract")  between  the City  of South  Gate  ("City")  and NR  Development,  Inc.
("Contractor").  This Addendum  constitutes  one of the Contract  Documents  identified  in Article
III  of the Contract.  All  capitalized  terms  used in this Addendum  shall have the same meanings
ascribed  to them in the Contract,  unless otherwise  defined  herein.  The agreements  set forth  in this
Addendum  are intended  to and shall have the same force  and effect  as if set forth  at length  in the
Contract.

The City  and Contractor  hereby  agree that the prices  specified  in the Contract  Documents  for the
following  Bid  Items  will  fully  compensate  Contractor  for performance  of the work  specified  in
those bid items,  as clarified  in paragraph  nos. l through  6 below:

1.  Bid  Item  No.  3: "Demolition  and  Site  Clearing"  includes  all  necessary  demolition  in
conflict  with  site  improvements  and per the Project  plans  and specifications.  No  additional
compensation  will  be given for demolition  items within  the captured  dashed line on the demolition
plan.  No additional  compensation  will  be made for any work  related  to this bid item.

2.  Bid  Item  No.  4: "Excavation  including  Export"  includes  the  excavation,  export,  and
disposal  of the asphalt  concrete  pavement  in the structural  section  on the street  and all asphalt
concrete  that is to be removed.  This  also includes  the asphalt  concrete  pavement  that is inside  the
park area that was previously  used as patch  work.  No additional  compensation  will  be made for
any work  related  to this bid item.

3.  Bid  Item  No.  28: "Electrical"  means  all  electrical  and lighting  work  for  the  Project.
Including  but not limited  to the following:  (a) all electrical  work  shown  on the Civil,  Architectural,
Structural,  and Mechanical  plans,  for the entire  Project;  (b) site lighting,  building  lighting,  and all
other  lighting  work  on the Project;  and (c) any and all other  electrical  work  as described  in the
Project  specifications.  Work  under  this bid item  shall  include  performing  all work  related  to the
electrical  work  including  but  limited  to furnishing  all  labor,  equipment,  tools,  materials,  and
services  to complete  the electrical  work  per the Contract  Documents.  This  also includes  all work
to comply  with  all provisions  of Title  24 requirements  as described  in the Contract  Documents.
No additional  compensation  will  be made for any work  related  to this bid item.

4.  Bid  item  No.  48:  This  bid  had  a discrepancy.  "Double  Swing  Entry  Gates-Includes
Decorative  Aluminum  Cut Panels",  will  be paid for as a unit cost of $20,046  per set. A total  of 3
sets are required  and therefore,  the total  amount  to be paid  is $60,138,  as indicated  on the bid
schedule.  Each set will  not be paid at the unit cost of $60,138  as indicated  in the bid.  No additional
compensation  will  be made for any work  related  to this bid item.

Business  & Professions  Code  § 7028.15:

  a.  It is a misdemeanor  for any person to submit  a bid to a public agency
  in order to engage in the business  or act in the capacity  of a contractor
  with in this state without  having a license therefor,  except in any of the
  following  cases:

  The person is particularly  exempted  from this chapter.
  The bid is submitted  on a state project governed  by Section 10164
  ofthePublic  Contract  Code  or on any local  agency  project
  governed  by Section 20104 [now § 20103.5] of the Public Contract
  Code.

  b.  If a person has been previously  convicted  of the offense described  in this
  section,  the court shall impose a fine of 20 percent of the price of the
  contract under which the unlicensed  person performed  contracting work or
  four thousand  five hundred  dollars  ($4,500),  whichever  is greater, or
  imprisonment  in the county jail for not less than  10 days nor more than six
  months, or both.

  In the event the person performing  the contracting work has agreed to
  furnish materials  and labor on an hourly basis, "the price of the contract" for
  the purposes  of this subdivision  means the aggregate  sum of the cost of
  materials  and labor furnished  and the cost of completing  the work to be
  performed.

  C.  This section shall not apply to a joint venture license as required by Section
  7029.1.  However, at the time of making a bid as a joint venture each person
  submitting  the bid shall be subject to this section with respect to his or her
  individual  licensure.

  d.  This section shall not affect the right or liability  of a licensed architect,  land
  surveyor,  or registered  professional  engineer  to form joint ventures  with
  licensed contractors  to render  services  within  the scope  of their respective
  practices.

  e.  Unless  one of the foregoing  exceptions  applies  a bid submitted  to a public

 BACKGROUND:  The Project  is part of the Capital  Improvement  Program  and was budgeted
 to improve  pedestrian  and vehicular  safety,  and relieve  traffic  congestion.  More  specifically,  the
 project  was to synchronize  18 traffic  signals  along  Tweedy  Boulevard,  between  Alameda  Street
 and Atlantic  Avenue.  The Project  entails  installing  conduit  and fiber  optic  cabling  to physically
 connect  traffic  signals,  traffic  signal  cabinets  and controllers,  battery  back-up  units,  closed  circait
 cameras,  video  detection  cameras,  traffic  loops and in-pavement  road lighting  at four un-controlled
 crosswalks.

 On June  23, 2022,  the Notice  Inviting  Bids  for
  construction was advertised  in various trade
publications,  the City's  website,  and in the local press. On August 4, 2022, eight bids were received
in the City  Clerk's  Office.

The bid  documents  included  a Base Bid  and an Additive  Alternate  Bid.  The bid  requirements
provided  that the lowest  bidder  be determined  based on the amount  of the Base Bid.  Belco  Elecnor
was the apparent  lowest  bidder,  with  a Base Bid
  (See Attachment  of $3,408,788.
  C.) However,
after analyzing  all the bids for mathematical  errors, the low bidder was determined  to be Servitek
Electric, Inc. The company's  corrected Base Bid was $3,264,364  and Additive  Alternate  Bid was
$703,223, for a total bid of $3,967,587. This bid is well over the engineer's
  estimate of $1,900,000
and exceeds the Project budget of $2,100,000,  and would require a budget of over $4 million.  This
budget level is not recommended  due to limited funding resources and warrants rejecting  the bids.

The Public  Works  Department  will  be rebidding  the project  with  a reduced  scope of work.  The
changes will  include:  (a) decreasing  the project  limits  to come up with  aproject  within  the allocated
budget  and grant funds,  and (b) eliminating  the improvements  on California  Avenue  which  are not
required  by the grant.  The Department  will  pursue  grant  funding  at a future  time  to attempt  to
acquire  funds to construct  the improvements  being  removed.

The South  Gate Municipal  Code has requirements  for rejecting  bids.  One requirement  is that the
bids be formally  rejected  by City  Council  action.  Another  requirement  is for the City  to fin-nisli  a
written  notice  to the apparent  low bidder  at least two days prior  to City  Council  rejecting  the bids.
The Engineering  Division  issued  such notice  on August  31, 2022,  to Servitek  Electric,  Inc. (See
Attachment  D.)

  responsible  for replenishing  ground  water.  He explains  that the water
  replenishes  naturally  to some levels,  but it also requires  to be replenished.
  So, when we draw water  from  underground  it must be replenished,  that is
  why they are paying  so much  for water.  Explains  that the alternative
  would  be to import  water but even importing  water  is also expensive.
  They  are in a predicament  because  they rely on groundwater  and there is a
  fee that must be paid to replenish  it.

  Mayor  Rios explains  that it is interesting  because  it is our water
  underground.  Asks if it belongs  to the city.

  Mr.  Cervantes  explains  that it is underground,  but water  ownership  is not
  contingent  upon location  within  a city it is based on water rights.  The city
  has water  rights  that allow  them to extract  water,  but they are also required
  to pay services  like replenishment  assessment.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  APPROVING  A  SHOP  LOCAL  DIGITAL  GIFT  CARD
PROGRAM  WITH  COMPONENTS  AJ'STDIMPLEMENTATION  MEASURES  TO  SUPPORT
LOCAL  MERCHANTS  IN SOUTH  GATE

PURPOSE:  To authorize  the City  Manager  to execute  agreements  to implement  a Shop Local/Gi:ft
Card program  utilizing  $115,000  in American  Rescue Plan Act funds.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Appropriating  $115,000  in American  Rescue  Plan  Act  (ARPA)  funds  for  the purpose  of
  implementing  a program  to support  local  businesses  located  within  the City  of South  Gate
  ("City"); and
  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to enter into  an agreement  with  Hinderliter,  de Llamas  and
  Associates,  Inc. (HdL  Companies),  for marketing,  administrative  and other services associated
  with the Digital  Gift Card Program  in an amount not to exceed $12,500;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the City Manager to enter into an agreement  with Yiftee,  Inc., for development  of
  the Digital Gift Card Program and merchant enrollment.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  will  be no expenditure  of General  Fund  dollars.  The funds  for the
program will  come from ARPA  funds  received  by the City  and used to support  small  businesses
located within  South Gate.

ANALYSIS:  The COVID-19  pandemic  has had numerous  negative  impacts  on communities,  and one
of the hardest  hit  sectors  has been  small  businesses.  Many  such  businesses  have  experienced
significant  financial  strains  due to the shutdowns,  labor  shortages,  and supply  chain inflation  costs.
Small businesses make up over 99% of businesses  in the nation  and account for 60 million  jobs.  Due
to the pandernic,  over 200,000 of those businesses  closed their  doors permanently  in 2020 and that
number continues  to rise two years later.

According  to a Spectrumnewsl  report  dated  February  5, 2021,  businesses  hit  the hardest  were
restaurants,  retail stores, bars, beauty salons, and gyms.  Women  and minority-owned  businesses were
the most vulnerable  during  the pandemic,  as these enterprises  tended to have less money  available  and
unsubstantial banking relationships,  making  it harder  to access capital  and other  funds through  the
Paycheck Protection Act.

  l

  343
 Small  businesses  in South  Gate have been hit hard due to these issues and continue  to stniggle.  Our
businesses  depend  heavily  on local  foot traffic  to be successful,  and the pandemic  has been especially
hard  on our  community  due to its economically,  disadvantaged  stahis.  It may  take  years  for  this
crucial  sector of businesses  to recover,  as it did from  the 2008-09  recession.

The  Digital  Gift  Card  Program  is an innovative  way  to stimulate  local  consumer  spending,  thereby
supporting  locally  owned  small  and independently  owned  businesses  in South  Gate.  Various  studies
show  that when  $100  is spent at a local  business,  nearly  $68 stays in the form  of taxes,  payroll  and
supplies  being  reinvested  into  the community  by the business,  as compared  to corporate  owned-non
locally  owned  businesses.

The  digital  gift  card platforms  have  been used by municipalities  for  several  years.  The three  main
companies  that provide  the platform  for  digital  gift  cards  are Faactor4,  Giverrang  and Yiftee,  with
Yiftee  being  the most  popular  and having  the best customer  service  rating.  Yiftee  is based  in Menlo
Park  in the  Silicon  Valley  and  is currently  doing  community  digital  gift  card  programs  in  many
Califomia  cities  including  Alameda,  Benicia,  Berkeley,  Brentwood,  Carlsbad,  Cupertino,  Dana  Point,
Fremont,  Hayward,  Lafayette,  La Verne,  Murrieta,  Livermore,  Oakley,  Pinole,  Redlands,  San Leandro,
and Vista  to name  a few.  Some of these cities  have been using  the program  for several  years  initially
funding  it with  CARES  Act funds  and then ARPA  funds.

The  Yiftee  Community  Digital  Gift  Card  program  is a cost-effective  way  to stimulate  the  local
economy  and assist small  businesses  in recovery.  It also provides  additional  savings  to resident's  who
shop locally.  As an example,  the proposed  digital  gift card program  would  have the resident  buy a gift
card valued  at $25, and the program  would  provide  another  $25 gift  card for a combined  $50 in gift
cards dollars  to be spent locally.  In other words,  it is a buy one and get one free for residents.

To initiate  the program,  the City  would  enter  into  Yiftee's  Community  Card  Customer  Agreement
(Exhibit  A).  There  is no set-up or monthly  costs.  The costs paid to Yiftee  are:

  1.  The value  of the bonus  card provided
  2.  The $1 plus 5% eDelivery  fee (purchaser  fee) plus a $1 gift fee per card
  3.  The Participating  Merchant  fees charged  by MasterCard

To assist with  the branding  costs  associated  with  the development  of the "Shop  Local  South  Gate"
campaign,  marketing  of the digital  gift  card (in English  and Spanish),  and related  signage  and posters
for  participating  businesses,  we  are proposing  an agreement  with  HdL  Companies  through  there
EconSolutions  division.  HdL  has partnered  and brought  this program  to several  of their  clients  over
the  last  year.  Those  clients  include  Hercules,  Hawthorne,  Canyon  Lake,  Lafayette,  Pinole,  San
Leandro,  and Oakley.  HdL  would  work  with  staff,  the Chamber  of Commerce,  and the Tweedy  Mile
Association  in these endeavors  to help  ensure  a successful  program.  HdL  Companies'  costs for their
services  would  be in a not to exceed  contract  of $12,500.  HdL  Companies  has been a critical  partner
with  the City  of South  Gate  providing  information  on sales tax,  property  tax  and business  license
services  for numerous  years.

The  pilot  program  was presented  to the South  Gate  Chamber  of Commerce  and the Tweedy  Mile
Association  representatives.  Both  groups  expressed  strong  support  for the program  and felt  it would
assist small  businesses  in these difficult  times.

 The  timeline  for  implementation  is about  8-12  weeks,  with  the  goal  of having  the  program  fully
operational  in time  for the holiday  shopping  season.  The digital  gift  card can only  be used at South
Gate businesses  and those  that  are independently  owned  (not  corporate  owned  nor  multi-franchisee
owned),  The  City  can limit  the type  of business  categories  that  can participate.  Most  cities  have
limited  the type of participating  businesses  to:

  1.  Retail
  2.  Restaurant/Cat6
  3.  Personal  Services  such as:
  a.  Hair  Stylists
  6.  Barbers
  c.  Estheticians
  d.  Nail  salons
  e,  Dry cleaners
  f.  Pet groomers
  g.  Fitness/specialty  studios,  including  martial  arts, yoga, dance, and music

The business  must  also operate  in a physical  storefront  location,  have a current  City  business  license,
and have no current  code enforcement  actions  pending  against  them.

The values  for the Digital  Gift  Cards will  include  $25, $50, and $100 amounts.

  APPENDIX  A - Pricing

Customer  and Participants  are not required  to pay Yiftee  a subscription  fee or a revenue  share.  Yiftee
does not take a percentage  of the cards that  are redeemed  in the Participants'  stores.

Charges:

Purchasers  pay the face value  of the card plus a 51+5% of the eGift Card value  eDelivery  fee at the time
of purchase.  Bulk purchases  of one thousand  dollars  (!>1000) or more,  and enterprise  accounts  may
qualify  for a reduced  eDelivery  fee by depositing  funds  into their  Yiftee  eGifting  accounts  by check or
ACH and disabling  credit  cards.

Participants  pay Mastercard  processing  fees for a card-not-present  (CNP) transaction  upon  redemption.
Yiftee  does not control  these  fees, they are set by the Merchant  Acquirer  who  is their  credit  card
processor.

Subject  to applicable  laws, Yiftee  will implement  a monthly  maintenance  fee on eGift Cards that  have
been inactive  (i.e. no spending  on the Card) for periods  of greater  than 12 months.  This will  be made
clear to cardholders  on the face of the eGift Card when  implemented,  as is required  by law.

Yiftee  eGift Cards do not generally  expire.  Subject  to applicable  laws, in some cases eGift  Cards given  by
corporations  or merchants  as promotions,  rewards  and awards  may have expiration  dates.  In the case of
eGift Cards expiring,  Yiftee  retains  10% of the original  eGift  Card value  not to exceed  the remaining
unspent  funds  and refunds  the balance  to the purchaser's  Yiftee  eGift  Card account.  eDelivery  fees are
not refunded.

Participants  may choose,  at their  discretion,  to post Offers  to encourage  Purchasers  to use their
Community  Cards in their  stores.

Participants  may choose,  at their  discretion,  to offer  rebates  as fund  raisers to local groups  such as
schools,  churches  and other  non-profits.  Such programs  are an incentive  for the local groups  to sell
Community  Cards to their  members,  and for the Purchasers  to use them  in specific  stores  who  are
offering  rebates.  Yiftee will work  with  the Participants  and Purchasers  to execute  such programs.

No tipping  is allowed  on Yiftee  eGift  Cards.

minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
CALL TO ORDER  Al Rios, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at 6:35
  p.m.

INVOCATION  Pastor Marta Moscoso, Faith and Hope Lutheran Church
PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Leslie Medina, Code Enforcement Supervisor

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Al Rios, Vice Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Council Member
  Maria Davila, and Council Member Gil Hurtado; City Treasurer Greg
  Martinez, City Manager Chris Jeffers, City Attorney Counsel Raul F.
  Salinas

ABSENT  Council Member Denise Diaz

1
PROCLAMATIONS  The City Council issued a Proclamation declaring the week of October 10
  - 14, 2022, as Code Enforcement Officer Appreciation Week in the City of
  South Gate.

RECESS  The City Council took a 5-minute recess.
2
PROCLAMATIONS  The City Council issued a Proclamation declaring the month of October
  2022, as National Domestic Violence Awareness Month in the City of
  South Gate.
3
PROCLAMATIONS  The City Council issued a Proclamation declaring the month of October
  2022, as Crime Prevention Month in the City of South Gate.
4
PROCLAMATIONS  The City Council issued a Proclamation declaring the month of October
  2022 as Breast Cancer Awareness Month in the City of South Gate.
COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Virginia Johnson explains that there were times from 2003-2016 that when
  they had a lot of people who had the same comments on the same items,
  they would allot time for the public to comment on the item. The practice
  stopped for some reason, and she asks if they could get this system again.
  Also suggests giving the 5 minutes back to residents. She thanked Leslie
  Medina from Code Enforcement for helping her neighbor about her lawn
  and giving her an extension.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  Jesus Miranda expressed how difficult it is to drive on Firestone
  Boulevard. Last time he talked about the difficulty to speak with the new
  time limit and the mayor talked about the surrounding neighborhood. He
  would like to see the Council Chambers full of people and is going to do
  something so that it can be full. Asks the Council to help the community
  by putting restrictions on Firestone Boulevard because it is a nightmare to
  park and drive from Long Beach Boulevard to Garfield. Talks about the
  time he spends getting through the different intersections and explains a
  lot of the issues he has noticed in these streets.

  Joe Pacheco stated submitting a petition to increase the police presences
  between State Street and Long Beach. Also thanks Chief Arakawa and the
  police department for their service, says they don't hear it a lot and talks
  about the current political climate. Says he had a lengthy call with the
  lieutenant from the police department about some of the issues in the
  community like graffiti, vandalism, and thief. Explains that after he
  submitted the petition, he got another call from the city. He explained that
  the city needed to conduct a survey of issues reported. He also explained
  that there was another application that needed to be submitted for a four
  way stop sign. He explained that there was a fee of 3,500 dollars and
  explains that this was never explained to him. Asks if there is a petition or
  a fee waiver. Also explains that they have discussed a stop sign on Long
  Beach Boulevard and he disagrees with the sting proposed, explains that
  the streets are narrow which makes it difficult for traffic and says an island
  is unnecessary.

  Mario Dominguez explains that at the last council meeting he was going to
  ask the council to make a motion to give the green light to the connector
  project. He has been speaking with a gentleman about this project and
  explains more regarding his efforts. Rest of the comments where not
  audible.

  Jose De La Paz comment is not audible.

  Thomas Buckley stated that this is good representation of the civic
  formalities and says the council did a great job considering everything the
  council was able to take care of Thinks it is a reasonable time for
  residents to speak, he used to be a critic of the time but now he thinks that
  it is sufficient time to speak. He thanked Mr. Jeffers and Mr. Salinas the
  Brown Act presentation and applauds their efforts. Also thinks that the
  meeting should have been recorded for the residents who were unable to
  attend.

  Page 2 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works explained that regarding the
  Firestone Boulevard traffic signal there is a level of synchronization effort,
  and that level is based on an older level of technology. The County of LA
  does have a enhance program to make the synchronization of Firestone
  Boulevard explains that it will create changes, but the level of change will
  not be drastic because it has lots of crossing streets.

  Mayor Avalos asks what is happening regarding the parking on Firestone.

  Mr. Cervantes explains that there is a competing interest, as the needs of
  the businesses compared to the needs and wants of the residents. The city
  applied for grants many years ago to apply it to Firestone Boulevard, the
  purpose was to convert it to two lanes permanently in each direction and
  not allow parking on either side of the street. When they initially began
  that project it became an issue and they needed to meet the requirements
  of the grants and of the residents. The businesses rely on the parking for
  business, as a result they have a third lane open during peak hours and the
  remainder of the time provides for parking. Explains that it was a long
  process that involved community outreach and that is how it led to the
  current design on Firestone Boulevard. Regarding the stop signs and
  humps, he explains the procedures that the city has when it comes to
  getting those in certain areas and where the funding would come from. He
  continues to go over the process when it comes to getting stop signs and
  the application as well as the fees.

  Mayor Rios asks if there is the potential that a medium in the middle of
  the road could take up another lane.

  Mr. Cervantes explains that the primary purpose for the median is to
  enhance circulation and safety. Explains that they are not making the
  medium wide enough to impact the traveling in the lanes, he provides an
  example of mediums that were created based off the original lane lines
  that were there.

  Greg Martinez, City Treasurer commented on the medium and some of the
  things he has noticed. For example, they are intended to prevent illegal
  turns and provides an example of people that do illegal stuff to miss
  traffic. He gets home late from working at the homeless shelter and he
  notes 3 or 4 times that there has been a homeless person come out and
  almost gets hit because they are unable to see them coming which is very
  dangerous. He explains that yes, they are trying to do some great things
  but there are circumstances where people do whatever they are going to do
  whether they are running late or any other reason. Explains that there are
  issues people face.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development has nothing to
  report.
  Page 3 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Steve Costly, Interim Director of Parks and Recreation reminded everyone
  that next week they will have a couple of events from Anthony Rendon's
  office that will be taking place, the first one is October 4th they will have a
  Latinx Pride event at the auditorium. On Wednesday they will be meeting
  people with the Meet and Great at the Rotary Club and the Second Annual
  Art Walk will be taking place on the 15th of October explains that it will
  be a good event and they have expanded the vendors.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works from public works has
  nothing to report.

  Kris Ryan, Director of Administrative Services has nothing to report.

  Chief Arakawa says that they are going to be educating the public on the
  dangers of fentanyl. They are working with the narcotics team and
  working on a presentation to educate the parents and students at school
  about the dangers of fentanyl, explains that it is a rising epidemic in Los
  Angeles County and neighboring communities.

  Mayor Rios asked if fentanyl is the cause of the overdoses that have
  happened recently.

  Chief Arakawa says that it is and that is why they are trying to hold a
  presentation.

  Vice Mayor Avalos asks if they will be carrying any Narcan or will just be
  having training.

  Chief Arakawa explains that they have not gotten to that discussion, but
  patrol officers do carry Narcan in the field and they are exploring the
  options for other field officers and city workers to carry and have that
  training. This is one of the options that they are exploring.

  Mayor Rios points out that there are school policies that have that and asks
  if it is true.

  Chief Arakawa explains that the school police do have it, but they are
  exploring the option of all city employees carrying some. Explains that the
  cost for Narcan is so little that it makes sense to look at other employees
  carrying it.

  Greg Martinez, City Treasurer says he carries Narcan and is trained. He
  explains that two fourth of Julys ago he saved one person at the homeless
  shelter, and he always keeps it in his backpack because they never know
  when they will need it. He thinks it is important for people to have it.
  Other than that, he has nothing to report.

  Page 4 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022

  REPORTS AND COMMENTS
  FROM CITY OFFICIALS
  CONT'D  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk has nothing to report but would like James to
  speak to see if everything is working on zoom.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager stated that there is a County Board Program
  called Land Banking Program. He will be happy to bring that back for
  discussion for the council. Explains that the program is the county
  working with metro to by land and bank it for affordable housing in
  specific public transporting areas and other project areas. The concerns
  with Eco-Rapid and other cities both along the Santa Ana line and other
  counties is that this could be done in conflict with local cities zoning and
  planning that could be ignored or altered through the county through that.
  This means they might not have a legal standing, or the local laws will not
  be enough to overtake what the county program is. He thanks Supervisor
  Hanh because she got on last minute a motion to try to modify the motion
  by saying that the city should be involved in the discussion being formed
  and it should be a decision to opt in. The motion failed but thanks her for
  her effort because she was responsive to the local cities including South
  Gate.

  Council Member Hurtado has a couple of items. He talked about the
  illegal dumping and explained that maybe the fee to get rid of it is high
  which is why they opt to dump it around the city. Explains they have a
  program and should try to educate residents or try a different approach.
  Regarding the traffic on Firestone explains that the city has taken steps to
  make the traffic better, explains that the street used to belong to the state
  of California.

  Councilwoman Davila asks the chief if he could add the church across the
  street from city hall. The pastor asked questions regarding the Narcan to
  see how it is used and to get educated, asks if they can include them in the
  information center.

  Chief Arakawa explains that the Narcan is used for fentanyl and heroin
  overdose, and it is simple to use.

  Councilwoman Davila says regarding the land banking, she understands
  that they cannot talk about it much because it will be brought up at another
  time. Explains that they need to talk about this because it allows metro to
  buy land and use it however, they want, and it should be opposed.
  Regarding the trip she mentioned to Washington D.C. it has been
  postponed to January of next year. The reason is because it is election
  time, and the legislators will not be there when they were looking to go
  which is why it has been postponed.

I
  Page 5 of 10
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Vice Mayor Avalos thanked Council Member Davila as well as Padres
  Unidos because they invited her to the meeting where the Superintendent
  as well as Jackie Goldberg was present at the meeting of Padres Unidos.
  She looks forward to working and collaborating with them to make sure
  that South Gate gets its fair share.

  Mayor Rios attended a Dia De La Mujer across the street, the church and
  city came together. They talked about breast cancer awareness, screening,
  and they would like to have more of these events. Also wants to remind
  people about the drought and the days they are allowed to water lawns
  along with some conservation tips.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works mentions that they have
  information on the South Gate city website, and they are also trying to do
  outreach every two weeks. He says the mayor did touch on a lot of the
  conservation tips and he also goes over some other tips that can help save
  water.

  Mayor Rios thanks Arturo Cervantes for doing outreach and says it is
  good to see the public here. He understands that covid is still out there and
  says they will be entering winter. Explains that they might have to wear
  masks in the winter because covid cases might go up and tells everyone to
  stay safe and be mindful and protect themselves.
